adopted: Agora routes redirect unauthenticated users to the branded /agora/auth entry while retaining the requested same-origin return path.
Agora and Pantheon Management share the same GCP Identity Platform user and BFF-verified browser session; Agora does not introduce a second credential store or password.
A first-factor Firebase identity remains visible while authoritative BFF verification is pending or rejected, and retry refreshes that same identity token before BFF readback.
TOTP enrollment refreshes the existing signed-in identity after enrollment instead of signing it out and requesting the same credentials again.

security_boundaries.authoritative_admission: Protected routes still require a VerifiedBffBrowserSession. A Firebase session alone, a BFF verification error, or a missing BFF session fails closed to the appropriate auth entry.
security_boundaries.credential_storage: No new credential persistence or browser-editable authorization claim is introduced. The existing in-memory Firebase-to-BFF bearer bridge remains the only registration path.
security_boundaries.redirect_safety: The auth page accepts only root-relative return targets and rejects protocol-relative targets before navigation.
security_boundaries.retry_behavior: Retry force-refreshes the current Firebase token and repeats authoritative BFF verification without silently admitting the first-factor identity.
security_boundaries.logout_behavior: Explicit account switching still clears both BFF and Firebase state; the single-sign-on change removes only the forced logout after successful TOTP enrollment.
